statement: For the curve $y=a^{x}$ with $a>1$, show that the tangent at $x=0$ has gradient $\\ln a$ and meets the $x$-axis at $x=-\\tfrac{1}{\\ln a}$.
solution: $y'=a^{x}\\ln a$; at $x=0$, $y=1$ and slope $\\ln a$. The tangent is $y-1=(\\ln a)x$. Its $x$-intercept satisfies $0-1=(\\ln a)x$, so $x=-\\tfrac{1}{\\ln a}$.
